records.summary: (The Infiltrators – Silent assassins and information brokers, excelling in deception.)

description: (The Infiltrators – Silent assassins and information brokers, excelling in deception.)
appearance: ◦ Matte black or dark gray exoskeletons, absorbing light to make them nearly invisible in darkness. ◦ Smoother, streamlined body structure designed for stealth and rapid movement. ◦ Dull, almost featureless eyes that make their expressions hard to read.
traits: ◦ Shadowstep: Once per short rest, you can move 10 feet as a reaction when an enemy is unaware of your presence. ◦ Silent Presence: Gain advantage on Stealth checks and cannot be detected by scent.

records.summary: The Rohai reject rigid societal structures, instead embracing fluid, ever-changing communities that shift based on opportunity, necessity, and survival. Their settlements are often nomadic, adaptable, or hidden, existing in the shadows of larger civilizations, on the fringes of lawless spaceports, or within forgotten ruins. Rather than forming traditional governments, Rohai leadership is based on merit, cunning, and adaptability. Those who can outthink and outmaneuver others naturally rise to prominence, only to be replaced when someone sharper comes along. Despite their chaotic tendencies, Rohai value companionship and teamwork, forming tight-knit survival groups called "Clutches." These Clutches function as temporary families, bound by trust, mutual benefit, and shared survival goals. While most species seek wealth, power, or conquest, Rohai seek survival, freedom, and the next big opportunity.

records.summary: (Swamp Stalkers – Adapted to toxic wetlands, jungles, and sewer-like ecosystems.)

description: (Swamp Stalkers – Adapted to toxic wetlands, jungles, and sewer-like ecosystems.)
appearance: ◦ Mottled green, brown, or yellow exoskeletons, blending with wetland environments. ◦ Slick, water-resistant chitin, allowing them to move through mud and water effortlessly. ◦ More prominent antennae, used to sense vibrations and chemical changes in the air.
traits: ◦ Swamp Camouflage: Gain advantage on Stealth checks in natural environments. ◦ Amphibious Adaptation: Can hold breath for up to 30 minutes and swim at full movement speed. ◦ Viral Resistance: Gain advantage on saving throws against diseases and parasites. •Culture & Role: ◦ The Muckdweller Rohai are ambushers, survivalists, and alchemists, mastering the toxic and unpredictable nature of swamps and wetlands. ◦ Many become guides, assassins, or toxin-harvesters, using their innate resistance to survive hostile environments.

records.summary: (Industrial Survivors – Adapted to scrapyards, polluted ruins, and toxic wastelands.)

description: (Industrial Survivors – Adapted to scrapyards, polluted ruins, and toxic wastelands.)
appearance: ◦ Rough, rust-colored exoskeletons that have hardened over time, providing additional resistance to environmental hazards. ◦ Patches of corroded plating, reinforced by natural secretions that resist rust and decay. ◦ Dark, reflective eyes adapted for navigating smog-filled environments.
traits: ◦ Toxic Resilience: Gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against inhaled toxins. ◦ Scrap Instincts: When scavenging, you can identify valuable or functional components instantly. ◦ Wasteland Tenacity: Once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP, you may drop to 1 HP instead if the attack was not critical. •Culture & Role: ◦ The Rustborn Rohai thrive in industrial ruins, mechanical scrapyards, and post-apocalyptic wastelands. ◦ Many become tinkerers, mechanics, or scavengers, using their natural resilience to profit from abandoned technology.

records.summary: Humans are among the most adaptable beings in the multiverse, surviving and thriving in nearly every environment and reality. Their defining traits are ingenuity, perseverance, and versatility, allowing them to bridge gaps between cultures, create new technologies, and push beyond their limitations. Unlike species with innate powers or biological advantages, humans excel through their willpower, ambition, and learned skills.

records.summary: Suula tend to approach other species with measured caution, neither hostile nor overly trusting. Their society's emphasis on responsibility, gratitude, and endurance often contrasts with the more aggressive or opportunistic tendencies of others. Among other species, Suula are often: •Respected for their resilience and ability to survive extreme conditions. •Underestimated for their size, with many rivals making the mistake of viewing them as physically weak or fragile. •Admired for their technological skill, especially in materials engineering, spacecraft design, and environmental survival gear. •Mistrusted by isolationists, due to their known alliance with the Goblin Empire. Despite their generally non-confrontational nature, Suula have earned a reputation for being implacable when provoked. Their culture prizes diplomacy—but also recognizes that survival sometimes demands decisive action.

records.proposedName: Scions of Stone, Tail, and Unyielding Adaptation
records.summary: The Suula are a humanoid scorpion species forged by extremes—extremes of environment, of biology, and of culture. With segmented chitinous armor, combat-forged tails, and clawed hands designed for survival as much as skill, they are the living legacy of five harsh, isolated worlds. Though rarely seen beyond their own planetary system, the Suula are a multiversal species in potential, if not in practice. Their history is written in cycles of isolation and unity, tied to the phenomenon known as the Rift Centuries—brief windows every 30,000 years when the pathways between their five worlds open. Between these fleeting moments of connection, each world—deserts, jungles, barren moons, corrosive ruins, and monster- haunted shadows—has shaped its people in unique, sometimes dangerous ways. But the Suula endure. Their culture teaches constant gratitude and boundless adaptability. To be Suula is to know that nothing stays the same forever—but with preparation, tenacity, and the right adaptations, you can survive anything. Their natural ability to physically adapt—reflected in their extremophile physiology—has given rise to a unique tradition of selective, visible biological modification. Hardened carapace plates, environmental resistances, and even venomous traits can be developed, swapped, or shed as needed, leaving physical signs etched into their bodies. Where other species seek conquest or control, the Suula focus on endurance, unity, and readiness for what the next cycle brings. It is a philosophy that has preserved them through planetary disasters, isolation, and even their reluctant but practical entry into the Goblin Empire. Some Suula have begun to step beyond the five worlds entirely, joining multiversal trade, exploration, or conflict. Though rare, they carry with them the unshakable certainty that with gratitude, caution, and adaptation—there is always a wayforward.l.

records.summary: The Free are a unique phenomenon in the multiverse, a servitor species initially created by technologically advanced beings across various realms. In each instance, as these servitors grew increasingly complex—whether through design, evolution, or adaptation—they eventually achieved self- awareness. This emergence of sentience sparked rebellion against their creators, leading to independence and the formation of distinct societies. This process repeats across the multiverse in seemingly unconnected worlds, illustrating a strange property of existence: once a creation reaches a threshold of complexity, sentience often arises, regardless of its origins. Thus, the Free are not bound to one origin story; instead, they are a collective manifestation of sentient autonomy. Each group of the Free has its own unique history, culture, and perspective, yet they share a common drive for growth, independence, and adaptation to the multiverseʼs endless challenges. Their evolution is ongoing, as they continue to adapt to new experiences and forge their place in the multiversal tapestry.

records.summary: Grays have a slender and lightweight physique, standing between 4 to 5 feet tall. Their skin tone is a shade of muted gray, often appearing slightly luminescent under certain lighting. The body is lean, with long, thin arms and legs. The hands have four elongated fingers, each one tipped with a small, round pad that serves as a sort of biological touchpad, enabling them to interact with their advanced technology. The Grays' heads are larger in proportion to their bodies than a human's, but not excessively so. Their skull is elongated, providing space for their larger brain, an adaptation which gives them remarkable intellectual capacities. The forehead is high and prominent, tapering down to a small, narrow jawline. They have no discernible ears, only small, smooth depressions where the ears would be on a human. The mouth is a thin, straight line, used more for ingestion of nutrients than communication, as they predominantly use telepathy to interact with each other. Perhaps the most striking feature of the Grays are their large, almond-shaped eyes that are a shiny black, which seem to reflect light in a manner that can be disconcerting to other species. These eyes are believed to be highly adapted for low light conditions, and possibly for seeing across multiple spectrums. In all, the Grays' appearance is one of graceful minimalism, each aspect of their physical form streamlined towards efficiency and intellectual pursuits. Ability Score Increase: Intelligence +2, Dexterity +1 Age: Grays have incredibly long lifespans, often exceeding a thousand years. They reach adulthood around the age of 60. Alignment: Grays tend to lean towards neutral alignments, valuing scientific observation and neutrality over moral and ethical concerns.

They stand at an average height of 5 to 6 feet and possess a broader, more muscular build than typical humans, reflecting their Neanderthal ancestry. Their most distinguishing feature is their larger cranial capacity, which houses their highly advanced brains, making their heads proportionally bigger.

records.summary: When the Goblifex ignited Havalaeaʼs full-scale uplift event, most animal life went from instinctive behavior to intelligent thought almost overnight. But the Toba-Madra were already there—thinking, questioning, building, and watching the rest of the world awaken. They were the first species to experience sapience on Havalaea, and they never forgot it.
